transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Um… mostly my sleep, I think. Since the warehouse inspection, I haven’t really been sleeping much. I know that maybe sounds… I don’t know, like a normal reaction or something, but I’ll lie there and bits of it keep replaying in my head.

And if I do fall asleep, I wake up sweating and completely wide awake, like I’m right back near that blast. I’m sorry, is that the kind of thing you mean?
Can you tell me a bit more about the warehouse inspection? Was there something about it that was particularly stressful or frightening for you?

Yeah… it was. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it was, but there had been a blast, and during the inspection I saw one of the workers on the floor. There was soot in the air and everything felt… unreal for a second.

And now, even during work, I’ll be reviewing a policy or looking at a loss report and suddenly that image just cuts in—him on the floor, the soot—and my body reacts before I can really stop it. Like I know I’m at my desk, but for a moment it doesn’t feel that way. Is that… is that the kind of detail you’re asking about?
Since the warehouse inspection, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?

A little, yeah… I mean, I’m still going to work and everything, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just refusing to do my job. But I’ve been kind of avoiding the warehouse file specifically.

And when emails about it come in, or industrial account calls pop up, I… I’ll let them go to voicemail more than I should. Even just opening those emails makes my stomach drop. I know that’s probably not ideal. Is that the kind of avoiding you mean?
Since the warehouse inspection, have you noticed yourself feeling more irritable, anxious, or emotionally numb than usual?

I guess… maybe more irritable than usual, yeah. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m taking it out on everyone, because I’m really trying not to.

But I did snap at a junior analyst over this tiny spreadsheet question, and it came out way harsher than I meant. Afterward I felt really embarrassed, because that’s not how I usually treat people. I apologized, but… yeah, that’s been bothering me.
Since the warehouse inspection, have you been feeling guilty about anything, even if you know it wasn’t your fault?

I don’t think so… not really guilt, exactly. I mean, I’ve wondered if I handled myself okay afterward, or if I’m making too much of it, but I don’t really feel like what happened was my fault.

I hope that makes sense. I’m not trying to dodge the question—I just don’t think guilt is the main thing for me.
Since the warehouse inspection, have you found yourself feeling ongoing fear, anger, or shame, even when you're not actively thinking about the event?

Um… I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I’m walking around feeling afraid or angry all the time, exactly.

Maybe a little on edge sometimes, but I don’t know if that counts as ongoing fear. And shame… I mean, I feel embarrassed talking about it, but I don’t think I’ve noticed a big constant feeling like that when I’m not thinking about the inspection. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any lasting feelings of fear, anger, or shame since the warehouse inspection, even when you’re not directly thinking about it?

I… I don’t think I’ve noticed that as a lasting thing, no. Like, if I’m reminded of it then I can feel uncomfortable, but when I’m just going through my day, I wouldn’t say I’m carrying around fear or anger or shame.

At least, not that I can clearly point to. I’m sorry if that’s not a very helpful answer.
Since the warehouse inspection, have you noticed yourself feeling detached from others or losing interest in activities you usually enjoy?

I don’t think so… not in a major way. I mean, I’ve maybe been a little quieter than usual, but I wouldn’t say I feel detached from people.

And I’m still doing the things I normally do, more or less. Maybe not with quite the same energy, but I don’t think I’ve lost interest exactly. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Since the warehouse inspection, have you found yourself feeling hopeless about the future or struggling to experience positive emotions like joy or happiness, even in moments when you'd expect to feel them?

I don’t think so… not hopeless, no. I mean, I’ve had moments where I’m kind of flat or distracted, but I can still laugh at things or enjoy little stuff if it’s happening.

I wouldn’t want to overstate it. I don’t feel like I’ve lost the ability to be happy or anything like that. Does that answer it okay?
Would you say you've been experiencing any ongoing feelings of fear, anger, or shame since the warehouse inspection, even when you're not directly thinking about it?

I think… no, not ongoing like that. I don’t really feel afraid or angry or ashamed when I’m just doing normal things.

If something makes me think about it, I can get a bit uncomfortable, but otherwise I wouldn’t say those feelings are just there all the time. I hope that makes sense.
Have you noticed any difficulty feeling positive emotions like happiness or joy, even in situations where you’d normally expect to feel them?

I don’t think I’ve really noticed that, no. Like, I can still feel happy if something good happens, or if someone says something funny.

Maybe I’m a little more distracted than usual, but I wouldn’t say joy feels blocked or anything. I’m not sure if that’s the right way to put it.
Since the warehouse inspection, have you noticed that your emotional reactions to things in general have changed—like feeling more negative or having a hard time feeling emotions the way you used to?

I don’t think there’s been a big change like that, no. I mean, I’m probably a little more on edge or distracted at times, but emotionally I still feel like myself, mostly.

I can still have normal reactions to things… I don’t feel like everything has turned negative or like I can’t feel things properly. At least, not that I’ve noticed. Is that what you mean?

Have you noticed any persistent changes in your mood or emotional reactions, such as feeling consistently down or having difficulty regulating your emotions, even when you're not thinking about the warehouse inspection?

I don’t think so, no. I haven’t really noticed myself being consistently down or out of control emotionally when I’m not thinking about it.

I mean, I might be a little tense sometimes, but mood-wise I think I’m mostly normal. If I’m answering that the way you mean.
Have you noticed any ongoing changes in how you feel emotionally—like feeling more negative or having trouble feeling emotions like you used to—since the warehouse inspection?

I don’t think so… not in an ongoing way. I mean, I’ve been a little shaken up by it, obviously, but I wouldn’t say I’ve become more negative overall or that I can’t feel emotions like I used to.

I still feel like myself emotionally, for the most part. If that makes sense.
Since the warehouse inspection, have you noticed yourself being more watchful or on guard, like you’re always looking out for danger, even when you’re not thinking about the event?

Not really, no. I mean, I might be a little more aware of things than usual, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly looking for danger or anything like that.

I don’t think I’m walking around on guard all the time. At least, I haven’t noticed that. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
How long have these experiences of reliving the warehouse inspection—like the images coming into your mind and your body reacting—been happening? Have they been going on for more than a month?

It’s been… about a week, I think. Since the warehouse inspection, when the explosion happened.

So no, not more than a month. It’s fairly recent. I hope I’m answering that clearly.
Have these symptoms, like reliving the event and feeling on edge, been happening almost every day since the warehouse inspection a week ago, or have they come and gone?

It’s been going on since the inspection, so… about a week now, ever since the explosion happened at the warehouse.

I don’t know if I’d say every single moment or anything, but it has been kind of there across the week. Does that answer what you’re asking?
